verdict_reason: The code computes Kriegeskorte et al.'s RSA(l, l+1) = rho_S(vec(D^(l)), vec(D^(l+1))) under both dissimilarity measures the manuscript names, and I REFUTE the still-open gpt-5.6-sol RED on direct measurement. Its claim is that a pure coordinate permutation Y = X[:, perm] must leave RSA unchanged and BLME's does not. It does. On CONTINUOUS data -- the paper's domain -- 300 random coordinate permutations of a 25x768 cloud give worst |1 - rho| of EXACTLY 0.000000000 under Euclidean RDMs and EXACTLY 0.000000000 under correlation-distance RDMs. On five shaped fixtures (25x768, 200x768, 7x7 integer, 40x8, 200x64) the X-vs-X[:,perm] value is 1.0 (or 0.9999999999999999 at n=200, the Spearman self-value) for both metrics, and permuting BOTH members of a real pair leaves the statistic BIT-IDENTICAL (rel +0.000e+00 in 10 of 10 cases). Under a stress search over 500 randomly generated TIE-DEGENERATE integer fixtures the Euclidean family -- which is the shipped headline -- is non-exact in 0 of 500 cases, worst |1 - rho| 0.000000000. Only the correlation-distance twin is non-exact (142 of 456 non-degenerate cases, worst |1 - rho| 0.008185986), and the released rsatoolbox is non-exact on the SAME class in a head-to-head (it returns 0.999806482824 and 0.999589294253 on fixtures where BLME returns 1.0, and 1.0 where BLME returns 0.999674849609), so that is float64 tie conditioning shared with the reference rather than a BLME deviation. The statistic is also EXACTLY invariant across the full campaign ladder for both metrics: 0.096093512150135 (Euclid) and -0.025736285958732875 (corrdist) at every one of 1e-30, 1e-25, 1e-13, 1, 1e13, 1e25 and 2.406159650500376e38, and at translations +1e3 and +1e6, all rel +0.0000e+00 -- it is a rank statistic, so the numerics that broke stable rank, CKA and homology cannot reach it.
comparable_reason: The adjacent family is a BLOCK-COUNT proxy. Re-decomposing ONE fixed end-to-end linear map (I + 0.25G on 60 points in 24 dimensions) into L equal blocks via the matrix L-th root -- the geometry at the endpoints is identical by construction -- moves rsa_adjacent_mean 0.964088795085 (L=4) -> 0.995582840646 (12) -> 0.999493730399 (36) under Euclidean RDMs and 0.965201471680 -> 0.995787144119 -> 0.999518565853 under correlation distance, while rsa_early_late is essentially invariant (0.690827014981 -> 0.690799964711 -> 0.690737904901, span 8.9e-5). Width behaves differently for the two families: zero-padding the same 40x8 pair to d = 32/128/1024 is an exact isometry and leaves the EUCLIDEAN statistic BIT-IDENTICAL (0.701249319304 at every width), but the correlation-distance twin moves 0.716195962998 (d=8) -> 0.765383673442 (32) -> 0.770329011060 (128) -> 0.771276390355 (1024), +7.69%, because Pearson correlation ACROSS COORDINATES is not padding-invariant. rsa_early_late over Euclidean RDMs is the one member that is both depth- and width-stable.
github_reason: Ran the installed rsatoolbox (Dataset -> calc_rdm -> compare(method='spearman')) head to head against BLME's pdist + spearmanr path, on this pass specifically on the coordinate-permutation fixtures the standing RED rests on. Six random tie-degenerate integer fixtures: BLME's Euclidean value is 1.000000000000 in 6 of 6 and rsatoolbox agrees at 1.000000000000 in 6 of 6; under correlation distance the two DISAGREE in 4 of 6 with neither systematically closer to the exact 1.0 (BLME 1.000000000000 vs rsatoolbox 0.999806482824; BLME 0.999674849609 vs rsatoolbox 1.000000000000; BLME 0.999863079345 vs rsatoolbox 0.999589294253). Prior rounds' 12-adjacent-gpt2-layer-pair head-to-head (worst |BLME - rsatoolbox| 2.220e-16 for both RDM types) is unchanged by this source state.
paper_reason: Kriegeskorte, Mur & Bandettini (2008, Front. Syst. Neurosci. 2:4) is a methods paper: it publishes RDM figures and correlation-distance matrices for fMRI and monkey IT recordings and zero numeric layer-to-layer Spearman values for a transformer, so no like-for-like scalar exists. The reproducible anchors are the reference implementation (2.220e-16 on real gpt2 layer pairs) and the identity RDM, where a layer against itself returns exactly 1.0 (measured 1.0 at n=25 and 0.9999999999999999 at n=200, the Spearman self-value).
confounds_reason: Structural, not merely correlational: holding the end-to-end map EXACTLY fixed and changing only the block count drives rsa_adjacent_mean from 0.964088795085 to 0.999493730399 (L = 4 -> 36), so the adjacent family reads n_layers directly. The correlation-distance family additionally carries a width mechanism (+7.69% under an exact zero-padding isometry from d = 8 to 1024) that the Euclidean family does not (bit-identical at every width). rsa_early_late over Euclidean RDMs is free of both (depth span 8.9e-5, width span exactly 0).
defects: CONDITIONING (shared with the released reference, unreachable on the paper's domain), rsa.py:206-226: exact correlation-distance ties are ranked from independently rounded float64 pdist outputs with no tie-stable canonicalization. Over 500 randomly generated tie-degenerate integer fixtures the correlation family is non-exact in 142 of 456 non-degenerate cases (worst |1 - rho| 0.008185986); the Euclidean headline family is non-exact in 0 of 500. rsatoolbox fails the same class in a direct head-to-head. On continuous data the invariance is exact (300/300 permutations at 0.000000000 for both metrics). Worth closing to match the reference's conditioning, but not a fidelity defect.

CODE/NAME, rsa.py:250 `_meta_n_degenerate_rows_jittered` names an operation the code no longer performs -- the round-3 correction REPLACED the jitter with NaN-nulling (rsa.py:193-195 sets X[_bad] = np.nan), so the key counts NULLED rows while its name says jittered. REFERENCE-POLICY DIVERGENCE (deliberate, documented), rsa.py:187-195: for an exactly constant row BLME propagates NaN like scipy's pdist(..., 'correlation'), while rsatoolbox MASKS the degenerate rows and returns a number. BLME's conservative choice is right for a quantity the definition leaves undefined, and the code records the divergence rather than asserting the reference agrees. I hit this branch 44 times in 500 random integer fixtures, so it is reachable, not theoretical.
